In this study, we report an iron-catalyzed nucleophilic C(sp3)─H activation/C─S coupling via iron nitrenoids, employing dioxazolones as nitrene precursors in conjunction with nucleophilic substitution by sulfur nucleophiles. To enable the use of sulfur nucleophiles in oxidative C(sp3)─H functionalization reactions, we developed a rationally designed phthalocyanine iron(II) catalytic system. Without the need for pre-functionalized sulfur reagents, a wide range of sulfur-containing moieties, including complex drug molecules, can be introduced, highlighting its utility in organic synthesis and drug development. Mechanistic studies revealed that electron-withdrawing substituents on the catalyst framework play a crucial role in suppressing undesired hydrogen atom transfer events associated with thiol species that promotes the C─S bond formation.

item.title: Organocatalytic [5+1] Annulation of Bisindoles With Aldehydes for Constructing Indole‐Fused Six‐Membered Rings
item.description:
The first organocatalytic [5+1] annulation of bisindoles with aldehydes has been achieved, enabling the synthesis of structurally diverse indole-fused six-membered rings in high yields. Moreover, this method could be extended to a three-component reaction through the in situ generation of bisindoles, providing a new synthetic protocol for indole-fused six-membered rings.


ABSTRACT

The organocatalytic [5+1] annulation of bisindoles as 1,5-dinucleophiles and aldehydes as 1,1-dielectrophiles was achieved. Using this method, a series of indole-fused six-membered rings were synthesized with generally good yields (up to 97%), providing a green and efficient approach for the construction of indole-fused six-membered rings. Furthermore, this method enabled a three-component reaction by in situ generation of bisindoles from indole and 2-indolylmethanol. This reaction represents the first [5+1] annulation of bisindoles under Brønsted acid catalysis, providing a new strategy for the construction of indole-fused six-membered rings.

item.title: Phosphonomethyl (Thio)Phosphonamidite Reagents for the Construction of Phosphonylmethyl Phosphono(Di)Thioate Mono‐ and Diesters
item.description:
A set of new phosphonomethyl (thio)phosphonamidite reagents is introduced to generate unprecedented pyrophosphate mimetics. The versatile P(III)-P(V) reagents allow for the construction of various pyrophosphate isosteres, and the applicability of the chemistry is illustrated in the assembly of a diverse set of stabilized CDP-glycerol and CDP-ribitol analogues.


ABSTRACT

A repertoire of phosphonomethyl (thio)phosphonamidite reagents has been developed to enable the controlled synthesis of phosphonylmethyl phosphono(di)thioate analogues of intrinsically labile pyrophosphates. Selective amidophosphonitylation of an alcohol or thiol of choice with a phosphonomethyl phosphonbisamidite allows access to four (thio)phosphonamidite reagents bearing three orthogonal protecting groups that can be chemoselectively addressed. These reagents were isolated in homogeneous form in yields up to 95% and applied in a sequence involving azole-mediated phosphonamidite coupling with an alcohol and successive in situ sulfurization of the PIII-PV intermediate, which affords protected phosphonylmethyl phosphono(di)thioate tetraesters. The coupling and sulfurization steps were monitored with 31P-NMR, revealing the nature of the key intermediates and corroborating the high efficiency of the coupling and sulfurization reactions. Immediate global deprotection or subsequent site-selective deprotection of the terminal phosphonate followed by a phosphonodiester condensation furnishes unprecedented phosphonylmethyl phosphono(di)thioate mono- and nonsymmetrical diesters, respectively. Using this method, we have assembled four nucleoside diphosphate analogs as well as a set of eight stable CDP-glycerol and CDP-ribitol mimics, all in multimilligram amounts.

item.title: Tuning Halide Induced Metastability in a [2]Rotaxane by Varying Axle, Crown Ether, and Employing Bistability
item.description:
A series of metastable [2]rotaxanes with the same slippage stopper and constitutionally different [23]crown ethers exhibited fluoride-selective metastability albeit varying extrusion kinetics. Imparting bistability to these metastable [2]rotaxanes provided the macrocycle an option to choose between extrusion and shuttling upon TBAF addition. Extrusion versus shuttling dynamics is found to be dependent on solvent polarity, concentration, and the lability of the macrocycle introduced.


ABSTRACT

4-isopropylphenyl slippage stopper has been used for developing a series of [23]crown ether incorporated metastable [2]rotaxanes via click reaction. Two [23]crown ethers that is, 23C7 and X23C7 are employed. The crown ether stationed at the ammonium site exhibited extrusion selectively in the presence of fluoride anion (TBAF) over TBAX (X = chloride, bromide, and iodide) due to TBAX exhibiting H-bonding with the neutral triazole moiety of the axle. Replacing 23C7 by X23C7 has enhanced the overall stability of the [2]rotaxane by reducing the impact of metastability. Imparting bistability to the metastable [2]rotaxanes by transforming triazole to methyl triazolium (MTA+) moiety, offers the crown ether to choose between shuttling and extrusion, touting this as a competition between the two phenomena switching and metastability. Surprisingly, TBAF addition reveals preferential extrusion in case of 23C7 incorporated bistable [2]rotaxane while preferential shuttling was observed with X23C7 incorporated bistable [2]rotaxane. Micromolar to millimolar concentration variation has a telling effect on the mode of responsiveness in a bistable [2]rotaxane with a slippage stopper. On the contrary, in polar medium (DMSO-d6), extrusion is the only mode of responsiveness observed by NMR spectroscopy.

item.title: Upgrading Type‐II Heterojunction to S‐Scheme Heterojunction for Enhanced Photocatalytic Toluene Oxidation Performance
item.description:
ABSTRACT

Construction of heterojunctions has been extensively applied to enhance the catalytic performance of TiO2-based semiconductor photocatalysts in the oxidation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). However, improper charge transfer directions in type-II heterojunctions often result in inadequate redox reactions for O2/·O2 − and OH−/·OH at lower potentials. In this study, a three-component heterojunction with multi-stage S-Scheme charge transfer was constructed by a self-assembled growth strategy, where CeO2 and WO3 were strategically deposited onto TiO2 nanosheets and applied to the photocatalytic oxidation of toluene. Catalytic performance evaluation revealed that the Ce-W/TiO2 heterojunction significantly enhanced the photocatalytic oxidation activity of toluene. Notably, Ce-W/TiO2 reached a mineralization rate of 98.4%, surpassing most other catalysts. Further systematic characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that the incorporation of CeO2 and WO3 not only broadened the photoresponse range but also optimized the charge transfer and surface reaction kinetics, thereby enabling the highest photocatalytic toluene oxidation activity on Ce-W/TiO2. This work highlighted the critical role of charge transfer pathways in TiO2-based semiconductor photocatalysts for toluene oxidation and provided valuable insights for the rational design of highly efficient photocatalysts for VOCs mineralization through heterojunction engineering.

item.title: A Homoleptic Copper(I) Acetylene Complex
item.description:
Ligand substitution of weakly coordinated N2 in [(N2)Cu{Al(ORF)4}] (RF = C(CF3)3) leads to the homoleptic acetylene complex [Cu(C2H2)3]+[Al(ORF)4]−, which was characterized by single crystal x-ray diffraction, NMR, and Raman spectroscopy, as well as by extensive quantum chemical calculations.


ABSTRACT

We report the synthesis and characterization of the Cu(I) complex [Cu(C2H2)3][Al(ORF)4] (1), which represents a very rare example of a homoleptic acetylene complex. 1 was synthesized from the dinitrogen complex [(N2)Cu{Al(ORF)4}] by simple ligand substitution. While the crystallographic description of 1 is complicated by an incommensurate modulated structure, the molecular connectivity could be unambiguously determined, and the identity of 1 was further confirmed by NMR and Raman spectroscopy as well as extensive quantum chemical calculations.

item.title: Anti‐Exfoliation and Stable Ni@S1@SiC Catalysts by In Situ Crystallization for Electrothermal Dry Reforming of Methane
item.description:
An in situ crystallization strategy is developed to fabricate robust Ni@S1@SiC structured catalysts for electrothermal dry reforming of methane. The catalyst achieves remarkable anti-exfoliation performance via strong interfacial adhesion, affording high stable near-equilibrium conversions and addressing a key deactivation barrier for industrial electrothermal catalysis.


ABSTRACT

Alkane utilization via direct cleavage of C─H bonds is highly industrially relevant yet is practically limited by high endothermicity. Electrothermal catalysis addresses this challenge by delivering internal Joule heating through the catalyst, offering direct, and efficient heat supply. However, the severe exfoliation related to the interfacial temperature gradient causes irreversible deactivation, severely limiting the applicability of electrothermal catalysis for industrial application. In this study, we developed an in situ crystallization strategy to fabricate a robust structured catalyst based on foamed silicon carbide (Ni@S1@SiC) that overcomes this limitation. This is achieved via hydrothermal crystallization of Ni-embedded zeolite directly on the SiC foam, resulting in a homogeneously grown and intimately bonded zeolite layer. The in situ crystallized Ni@S1@SiC exhibits weight losses of less than 5 wt% in harsh exfoliation tests, much lower than the conventional washcoated catalyst (45.4%–91.8%). The durability of Ni@S1@SiC was exemplified in electrothermal dry reforming of methane (EDRM), presenting stable operation at 800°C at high conversions (93.2% for CH4 and 97.3% for CO2) and exfoliation of merely 3.6 wt%. This work provides a universal design principle for developing stable electrothermal catalysts, addressing the severe deactivation issue by exfoliation and paving the way for industrial application in endothermic reactions.

item.title: Hydrophilic–Hydrophobic Balance Regulates Aggregation and Red/NIR Fluorescence of Carbohydrate‐Conjugated Ar,O‐BODIPYs
item.description:
Carbohydrate-conjugated Ar,O-BODIPYs exhibit bright red/NIR fluorescence in organic media but form nonfluorescent aggregates in aqueous solution. Protein binding disrupts the aggregates and restores fluorescence, while optimized hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance enables efficient cellular uptake and high-performance bioimaging.


ABSTRACT

Aggregation-responsive fluorescent probes are attractive for biological applications because molecular recognition can be transduced into optical signals through changes in molecular assembly. In this study, we report a series of carbohydrate-conjugated Ar,O-BODIPYs that exhibit red/near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence responsive to their aggregation state in aqueous media. The carbohydrate-conjugated Ar,O-BODIPYs were readily synthesized by copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition. Although the compounds exhibited intense fluorescence in DMSO, their fluorescence was strongly quenched in aqueous media. Dynamic light scattering, atomic force microscopy, and fluorescence lifetime measurements revealed that this quenching was associated with the formation of nanoscale aggregates. Importantly, the extent of aggregation and fluorescence quenching depended on the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance between the Ar,O-BODIPY core and the appended carbohydrate moieties. Binding of a carbohydrate-conjugated Ar,O-BODIPY to concanavalin A induced a pronounced fluorescence enhancement, indicating that protein binding promotes disruption of the quenched aggregates. Among the compounds examined, the glucose-conjugated derivative showed the highest fluorescence intensity in living cells and efficiently stained several cell lines in the red/NIR region. These results demonstrate that controlling the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance provides a useful molecular design strategy for tuning aggregation, fluorescence response, and cellular uptake, enabling carbohydrate-conjugated Ar,O-BODIPYs to function as aggregation-responsive fluorescent probes for protein recognition and bioimaging.

item.title: Polycarbonate Upcycling Into Block Copolymers via Transcarbonation: Influence of the Catalyst on the Microstructure
item.description:
Upcycling of polycarbonate (PC-BPA) into PC-BPA–polybutadiene (PBd) block copolymers was achieved by transcarbonation with hydroxytelechelic PBd (Krasol) using organic base catalysts. Catalyst choice governed conversion, molecular weight and microstructure: TBD produced multiblock copolymers, whereas DMAP yielded higher M n materials with lower conversion and mainly diblock structures.


ABSTRACT

The upcycling of plastics into high-value materials has emerged as a promising strategy to handle plastic waste. The production of block copolymers is an interesting route. This can be done by polymer / polymer interchange reaction, where telechelic polymers can play a pivotal role. The work describes the upcycling of aromatic polycarbonate (PC-BPA) into PC-BPA-Polybutadiene (PBd) multiblock copolymers. The copolymers are synthesized via a transcarbonation reaction between hydroxytelechelic polybutadiene (PBd) and PC-BPA using N-heterocyclic bases as catalysts. A deep analysis of their microstructure is realized by NMR. The true formation of the copolymers is confirmed by DOSY experiments. It is shown that the nature of the catalyst strongly influences the microstructure of the resulting copolymers: TBD (1,5,7- triazabicyclo[4.4.0]dec-5-ene) provides high conversions and yields multiblock copolymers, while DMAP (4-dimethylaminopyridine) affords higher molecular weights materials with lower conversions and predominantly diblock structures. The PBd content of the latter copolymers is much lower than that of the former. As consequence, the thermal properties also differ. This work provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first report of PC-BPA/PBd multiblock copolymers.

item.title: Synthesis of Heteroatom‐Doped Macrocycles for OLED Applications
item.description:
This review highlights the synthesis of heteroatom-doped macrocycles via Pd-catalyzed couplings, base-catalyzed substitutions, and Lewis acid-catalyzed reactions, and their application in organic light-emitting diodes.


ABSTRACT

Heteroatom-doped macrocycles have emerged as a versatile platform for organic optoelectronics, particularly in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). By incorporating heteroatoms such as N, O, S, B, and Si into macrocyclic frameworks, researchers can precisely modulate electronic structures, band gaps, and photophysical properties. Compared to their linear counterparts, macrocyclic emitter's offer enhanced rigidity, which suppresses conformational disorder and vibrational relaxation, leading to higher photoluminescence quantum yields and more efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). The fixed topology also enables precise control of donor-acceptor spatial arrangements, facilitating efficient reverse intersystem crossing and improved exciton utilization. This review summarizes recent advances in the synthesis of heteroatom-doped macrocycles, focusing on three key strategies: palladium-catalyzed C–N coupling, base-catalyzed nucleophilic substitution, and Lewis acid-catalyzed Friedel-Crafts alkylation. Post-synthetic functionalization further expands the structural and functional diversity of these macrocycles. We also highlight the application of these materials in high-performance OLEDs and provide an outlook on the challenges and opportunities in this rapidly evolving field.

item.title: Structurally Diverse 6‐Amino‐2,3‐naphthalimides: Synthesis, Solvatochromic Properties, and Utility in Cellular Imaging
item.description:
A general route to access structurally diverse fluorescent 6-amino-2,3-naphthalimides has been developed, allowing for the facile functionalization of both the imide and 6-amino moiety. Microscopy experiments highlight their potential as fluorescent probes for bio-relevant imaging.


ABSTRACT

The burgeoning reliance on fluorescence techniques to detect analytes of interest and visualize cellular processes has heightened the need for synthetic approaches to readily access new and underrepresented fluorophore classes, including those based on the 2,3-naphthalimide scaffold. To address the lack of robust synthetic methodology, a general route to access structurally diverse fluorescent 2,3-naphthalimides has been developed. Following the synthesis of the key 6-bromo-2,3-naphthalic anhydride building block, imide formation and subsequent amination via Buchwald–Hartwig cross-coupling methodology afforded a number of 6-aminonaphthalimides with solvatochromic properties. Microscopy experiments in A549 cells highlight their potential as fluorescent probes for bio-relevant imaging, with a 6-piperazino-2,3-naphthalimide variant demonstrating pH-responsive fluorescent behavior via photoinduced electron transfer.

item.title: Highlighting Nuclear DNA in Live Cells With an Activatable BODIPY–Hoechst Conjugate
item.description:
Supramolecular association of a Hoechst ligand to double-stranded DNA activates the fluorescence of a connected BODIPY fluorophore. The resulting fluorescence enhancement enables the imaging of the cellular nucleus with negligible background emission from the extranuclear space in live cells under excitation in the green portion electromagnetic spectrum, ensuring negligible autofluorescence and photodamage.


ABSTRACT

The development of fluorescent probes to image the nucleus of live cells with high contrast and negligible photodamage is essential to overcome the limitations of existing nuclear stains and enable the visualization of chromatin dynamics with minimal perturbations on cellular functions. To this end, we synthesized a molecular construct integrating a borondipyrromethene (BODIPY) fluorophore and a Hoechst ligand within its covalent skeleton. In organic solvents, the Hoechst ligand has negligible influence on the photophysical properties of the BODIPY component. However, the characteristic fluorescence of the latter chromophore is completely suppressed in aqueous environments. Binding of the Hoechst ligand to double-stranded DNA inhibits the quenching pathway to activate fluorescence. As a result, our fluorophore–ligand construct allows the imaging of nuclear DNA in live cells with no background fluorescence from the extranuclear space under excitation wavelengths in the green portion of the electromagnetic spectrum, ensuring minimal autofluorescence and photodamage.

item.title: Converting Nylon Microplastic Waste to Value by Amphiphilic Lewis‐Acid Surfactant Catalysis
item.description:
The amphiphilic C10DOTA_Sc catalyst localizes a water-stable Sc3 + Lewis acid at the Nylon-water interface, enabling the aqueous conversion of Nylon-6, Nylon-6.6, and Nylon-12 microplastics into soluble molecular products under mild conditions.


ABSTRACT

Microplastics are pervasive pollutants that accumulate across environmental compartments and resist degradation under environmentally relevant conditions. Polyamide-based microplastics, particularly Nylons, are among the most persistent classes due to their densely hydrogen-bonded amide backbones, which limit accessibility and hinder degradation in aqueous environments. Existing purification approaches typically rely on energy-intensive thermal processes, harsh chemical conditions, or slow biological pathways. Here, we show that a surfactant catalyst comprising a ligand-Sc3+ complex as a Lewis-acidic headgroup can decompose nylon microplastics into their monomers, which may be returned to the chemical value chain. The comparison to non-amphiphilic reference catalysts proves that the surfactant character is a decisive factor, as it ensures that the catalytic core is in close proximity to the polymer chain. The surfactant catalyst removes microplastic particles from an aqueous environment, which was shown for Nylon-6, Nylon-6.6, and Nylon-12. The sustainability of the process is further improved because the surfactant catalyst can be isolated without losing any scandium and then reused.

item.title: Photoinduced Surface‐Generated Pt Complexes on Delayed‐Fluorescent Benzothioxanthene Imide Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
How can organic nanoparticles be transformed into hydrogen-producing photocatalysts? Light triggers a surface transformation of benzothioxanthene imide nanoparticles creating sites for platinum coordination, turning light-harvesting nanoparticles into catalytic systems. Their excited states with microsecond delayed fluorescence provide more time for productive charge transfer, while carefully controlled reaction conditions sustain hydrogen evolution over four days.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic hydrogen evolution (HER) using organic photosensitizers and platinum co-catalysts offers opportunities for sustainable hydrogen production, although operational stability and efficient Pt utilization remain challenging. Here, we investigate BTI-TPA, a donor–acceptor benzothioxanthene imide derivative, as a photoactive scaffold for Pt-based HER catalysts. Using unique photoreaction of imide fragment, BTI-TPA nanoparticles were functionalized with Pt complexes via in situ formation of mono- and binuclear Pt species. Photophysical studies revealed delayed fluorescence in such systems, which confirmed storing of the excitation energy for a few microseconds. Both prompt fluorescence (PF) and delayed fluorescence (DF) undergo dynamic quenching upon Pt coordination in the presence of sacrificial electron donors, suggesting energy transfer towards catalyst. The optimal catalyst with 10 mol% Pt relative to the BTI dye achieved a turnover frequency (TOF) of 55 h−1, while a 20 mol% Pt loading yielded the highest H2 production rate of 2.9 mmol g−1 h−1. With a HER activity retained over 50% after 4 days of continuous irradiation, this particular Pt based hybrid photocatalytic systems represent a rare type of surface-anchored molecular catalyst, in which mononuclear Pt species outperform their di- or oligonuclear derivatives.

item.title: A Hypoxia‐Activated Diketopyrrolopyrrole‐Based Single‐Molecule Prodrug for Combined Chemotherapeutic and Type‐I Photodynamic/Photothermal Trimodal Cancer Therapy
item.description:
This study develops a single-molecule prodrug for hypoxia-activated chemotherapy, photothermal therapy (PTT), and type-I photodynamic therapy (PDT) to selectively eradicate cancer cells.


ABSTRACT

Hypoxia, as a unique tumor microenvironment, offers an opportunity for the development of activatable therapeutic agents. However, most current activatable agents are confined to monotherapy, limiting their overall efficacy. We herein report a novel single-molecule prodrug for hypoxia-activated trimodal cancer therapy. A diketopyrrolopyrrole-based molecule (AMO) was first synthesized, demonstrating efficient type-I photodynamic (PDT) and photothermal (PTT) activities. To integrate chemotherapy, a hypoxia-cleavable azo linker was introduced to conjugate a cytotoxic drug, nitrogen mustard, yielding the prodrug AIO. Under normoxic conditions, the AIO exhibited attenuated phototherapeutic effects, minimizing off-target toxicity. In contrast, the hypoxic tumor environment triggered azo cleavage, releasing the chemotherapeutic agent while simultaneously restoring type-I PDT and PTT functionalities. This work provides an activatable trimodal combination therapeutic strategy with promising translational potential for precise cancer treatment.

item.title: Mechanisms, Performance Enhancement, and Future Challenges of Activation Processes in Spent Lithium‐Ion Battery Electrode Recycling
item.description:
Activation strategies have been developed to enhance spent battery recycling. This review categorizes these strategies into thermal, electron-beam, chemical, electrochemical, mechanical, and composite types, explaining their thermodynamic and kinetic mechanisms. It also compares their effects on recovery performance, resource use, environmental impact, and practical applications. The review provides insights and design principles for creating efficient, low-carbon, closed-loop recycling technologies for spent lithium-ion batteries.


ABSTRACT

The rapid retirement of lithium-ion batteries driven by electric vehicle growth poses substantial challenges to strategic metal supply security and environmental sustainability. Conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical recycling routes are often limited by high energy consumption, secondary pollution, and insufficient lithium recovery. Activation strategies have emerged as mechanism-guided approaches to improve spent battery recycling by regulating electrode structure, metal valence states, interfacial electron transfer, and reaction microenvironments. However, the shared activation principles, performance boundaries, and scale-up constraints across different activation processes remain insufficiently integrated. This review systematically classifies activation strategies into thermal, electron-beam, chemical, electrochemical, mechanical, and composite categories, and elucidates their underlying thermodynamic and kinetic mechanisms. It further compares their documented impacts on recovery performance, resource consumption, environmental footprint, and practical application scenarios. Representative studies show that activation can accelerate reaction kinetics, enhance selective metal extraction, and reduce energy or reagent inputs compared with conventional processes. In particular, multi-field composite activation provides opportunities for processing heterogeneous industrial black mass through synergistic regulation of reaction pathways. By clarifying challenges associated with material heterogeneity, impurity interference, reactor-scale implementation, and environmental-economic evaluation, this review establishes mechanistic insights and design principles for developing efficient, low-carbon, and closed-loop recycling technologies for spent lithium-ion batteries.

item.title: The Structure Optimization of Indenoquinoxalinone‐Based Novel Deep‐Red Emitters for OLEDs With External Quantum Efficiency Achieving 16%
item.description:
In this work, two deep-red TADF emitters are designed and synthesized. The T-shaped isomer 14-IQ achieves a maximum EQE of 16.0% with electroluminescent peak at 633 nm and a maximum luminance of 5736 cd m− 2 in device, substantially outperforming the Y-shaped counterpart 23-IQ across all efficiency metrics.


ABSTRACT

Developing efficient deep-red thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters remains challenging. Herein, using 11H-indeno[1,2-b]quinoxalin-11-one (IQ) as the electron acceptor and triphenylamine (TPA) as the electron donor, two isomeric emitters, Y-shaped 23-IQ and T-shaped 14-IQ were constructed by introducing TPAs at the 2,3- and 1,4-positions of IQ, respectively, enabling a systematic comparison of the influence of molecular structure on photoelectric properties. Both emitters exhibit small singlet-triplet energy gaps (∼0.13 eV); however, 14-IQ uniquely possesses a high-lying locally excited triplet (3LE) state that facilitates faster reverse intersystem crossing (RISC). Consequently, device based on 14-IQ achieved a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 16.0% with electroluminescent peak at 633 nm and a maximum luminance of 5736 cd m−2, substantially outperforming 23-IQ (EQE = 9.6%). This work underscores that the T-shaped 1,4-substitution pattern on the IQ core represents a promising molecular design strategy for developing high-performance deep-red TADF emitters.

item.title: Chiral Gold Nanofibers as Substrates Toward SERS‐Based Chiral and Flexible Sensing
item.description:
High-aspect-ratio chiral gold nanofibers are a recently reported low-dimensional material with intrinsic chiroptical properties. Here, we use them as label-free SERS substrates for the identification of enantiomers in mixtures and detection of model compounds on the surface of paper chip-based platforms.


ABSTRACT

Chiral plasmonic nanostructures offer unique opportunities for combining surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) with enantioselective molecular recognition. However, their integration into practical sensing platforms remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate high-aspect-ratio chiral gold nanofibers as versatile substrates for sensitive, chiral, and flexible SERS sensing. Using trans-1,2-bis(4-pyridyl)ethene as a model analyte, the chiral gold nanofibers enable molecular detection down to 1 nM and exhibit higher SERS efficiency (between 2–3× higher) than benchmark nanomaterials such as chiral and achiral gold nanorods. Beyond molecular detection, the chiral gold nanofibers provided indications of composition-dependent discrimination between D- and L-cysteine in mixtures with different enantiomeric compositions above analyte concentrations of, at least, 10 mM. Finally, the chiral gold nanofibers retain their SERS activity after integration into low-cost, flexible paper scaffolds, enabling spatial mapping and recovery of characteristic molecular fingerprints across the heterogeneous surface. These results establish chiral gold nanofibers as potential multifunctional plasmonic building blocks that combine molecular sensitivity, enantioselective recognition, and compatibility with flexible surfaces, providing a route toward adaptable platforms for label-free chiral sensing.

item.title: Thermodynamic Insights on Isodesmic Perylene Bisimide Dye Aggregation From Concentration‐, Solvent‐ and Temperature‐Dependent Studies
item.description:
The reliability of solvent- and temperature-dependent UV–vis absorption studies was assessed for the isodesmic self-assembly of a perylene bisimide (PBI), considering the solvatochromic and thermochromic effects for this chromophore. The obtained thermodynamic parameters are compared to reference values from the concentration-dependent analysis.


ABSTRACT

Solvent- and temperature-dependent self-assembly studies are often applied as alternatives to concentration-dependent analysis of supramolecular polymerization. However, spectral changes due to (de)aggregation are overlaid by solvatochromic or thermochromic effects, respectively, that can have significant impacts on the fit analysis. Here, a non-aggregating N,N’-2,6-diisopropylphenyl-substituted perylene bisimide (PBI) was studied in eleven solvents from 283 to 363 K, to acquire information on the impact of solvent and temperature on absorption properties. Subsequently, isodesmic aggregation of a PBI chromophore was studied in different solvent mixtures of toluene and 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane, CHCl3, or 1,2-dichlorobenzene, revealing that even small solvatochromic effects can significantly falsify data analysis, and derived thermodynamic parameters highly depend on the wavelengths chosen for data analysis. This wavelength-dependency and deviation of fit results from concentration-dependent reference values was also found in the temperature-dependent study due to varying degrees of thermochromism at different wavelengths. Still, if evaluated carefully by proper selection of suitable wavelengths, both methods can give reasonable results. The present example serves to illustrate the accuracy one can expect from the different methods and the reliability of thermodynamic parameters from concentration-, solvent-, and temperature-dependent UV–vis studies for one of the most studied dyes in the field of self-assemblies and supramolecular polymers.

item.title: A Mechano‐Electrochemical Stable Hydrogel for Flexible Energy Storage and Motion Monitoring
item.description:
A multifunctional P(AM-co-SBMA)/CMCS-IL hydrogel integrates high stretchability, compression resistance and ionic conductivity. Serving as an electrolyte for flexible supercapacitors, it exhibits a specific capacitance of 151.6 F g− 1 and an energy density of 21.06 Wh kg− 1, operates within a temperature range of −20°C to 60°C, and enables flexible strain sensing for human motion monitoring.


ABSTRACT

Balancing mechanical toughness, environmental durability, sensing accuracy in hydrogel based flexible devices remains challenging. This paper reports a multifunctional hydrogel P(AM-co-SBMA)/CMCS-IL, synthesized via free radical polymerization in [EMIM][BF4]/H2O binary solvent system, natural polysaccharide CMCS as rigid reinforcing network, AM and zwitterionic SBMA for flexibility. The hydrogen bonds provide exceptional tensile properties, enduring 961% strain and 80% compressive strain without fracturing. It exhibits strong dehydration resistance, retaining 80% of its water content after 12 h in room temperature environment. When assembled into FSC, the device has high specific capacitance of 151.6 F g− 1 at 0.2 A g− 1 and energy density of 21.06 Wh kg− 1 at 200 W kg− 1, while maintaining 76% capacitance retention after 8,000 cycles. Crucially, the FSC shows outstanding electrochemical stability across different bending (0° to 180°) and wide temperature range (−20°C to 60°C). Additionally, a flexible strain sensor based on the hydrogel features rapid electromechanical response (response and recovery times of 0.7 s and 0.6 s) and captures bending deformations and subtle muscle activities with high signal to noise ratios. This multifunctional electrolyte provides a key design strategy for integrating smart skins and flexible energy storage systems.

item.title: From Installation to Editing: The Rise of d3‐Deuteromethylation
item.description:
Trideuteromethylation has evolved from conventional installation to versatile catalytic and hydrogen-deuterium exchange strategies, enabling selective isotopic editing of complex molecules. This review highlights recent advances in CD3 reagent design, versatile catalytic and site-selective hydrogen-deuterium exchange, while outlining key challenges, mechanistic insights, and emerging opportunities.


ABSTRACT

The site-selective incorporation of deuterium into biologically active molecules has emerged as a powerful strategy for tuning the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties of pharmaceuticals. Among various deuterated motifs, the d 3-deuteromethyl (CD3) group has gained particular attention as a privileged pharmacophore, highlighted by its presence in three of five deuterated drugs approved thus far. By uniting the beneficial “magic methyl effect” with the kinetic isotope effect imparted by deuterium, d 3-deuteromethylation can effectively reduce metabolic liabilities while preserving biological activity, leading to improved pharmacokinetic performance and enhanced therapeutic potential. In recent years, the development of novel CD3-containing reagents, together with advances in photocatalytic and electrocatalytic methodologies, has enabled the efficient installation of CD3 groups with high selectivity under mild conditions. In parallel, hydrogen–deuterium (H-D) exchange strategies enable precise d 3-deuteromethylation at specific sites (such as α-thio C(sp3)─H bonds and benzylic C(sp3)─H bonds), providing a complementary approach to isotopic incorporation. This review summarizes the major advances in d 3-deuteromethylation over the past five years (from 2021 to 2026), with a particular focus on the design of novel CD3 reagents, the application of H-D exchange strategy in d 3-deuteromethylation, and the mechanistic principles underlying these transformations.

item.title: Asymmetric Reductive Homocoupling of Isatin Imines Templated by Chiral Diboron
item.description:
An efficient asymmetric reductive homocoupling of isatin imines is developed with a chiral diboron template, affording chiral vicinal diamines bearing 3,3′-bisoxindole scaffolds in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The reaction features mild conditions and signifies the broad applicability of diboron-participated [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement on functionalized ketimines.


ABSTRACT

An efficient asymmetric reductive homocoupling of isatin imines is developed with a chiral diboron template, affording the corresponding chiral vicinal diamines bearing 3,3′-bisoxindole scaffolds in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The reaction features mild conditions and is compatible with various substitution patterns, signifying the broad applicability of diboron-participated [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement for the first time on functionalized ketimines. The unstable nature of chiral vicinal diamine products bearing 3,3′-bisoxindole scaffolds, which are prone to undergo retro-Mannich reaction, complicates the reaction.

item.title: Enhancement of Electrochemical Performance of Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries Using Hydrated Eutectic Electrolytes
item.description:
Hydrated eutectic electrolyte reduces H2O content, inhibits HER, and widens electrochemical stability window to 2.61 V. Lower freezing point of electrolyte, enables symmetrical cell to operate stably for 800 h at −10°C. Zn||MnO2 cell retains a discharge specific capacity of 192.3 mAh g−1 after 2200 cycles at 1 A g−1, with a capacity retention rate as high as 92.3%.


ABSTRACT

Among various energy storage systems, zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) have emerged as promising candidates due to their inherent advantages, such as a low redox potential (−0.763 V vs. SHE), high safety, environmental benignity, high theoretical capacity (820 mAh g− 1 or 5855 mAh cm− 3), and low cost. With the rapid development of renewable energy technologies, the demand for ZIBs with high capacity, high voltage, and stable output performance continues to increase, placing increasingly stringent demands on electrode materials and electrolyte systems. This work aims to enhance the performance of ZIBs through electrolyte modification and zinc anode optimization. We engineered the electrolyte through the construction of a hydrated eutectic electrolyte by introducing acetonitrile (AN) as a co-solvent and formamide (FA) as a functional coordinating molecule. The strong coordination interaction between FA and Zn2 + effectively displaces coordinated water molecules from the Zn2 + solvation sheath, thereby suppressing hydrogen evolution reactions during cycling and widening the electrochemical stability window of the electrolyte from 2.52 to 2.61 V. The unique solvation structure and reconstructed hydrogen-bond network significantly decrease the freezing point of the electrolyte, enabling Zn||Zn symmetric cells to operate stably for 800 h at −10°C. Furthermore, the hydrated eutectic electrolyte promotes reversible Zn2 + intercalation/deintercalation in MnO2. Consequently, the assembled Zn||MnO2 full cell achieves a discharge specific capacity of 192.3 mAh g− 1 and maintains 92.3% capacity retention after 2200 cycles at a current density of 1 A g− 1.

item.title: Direct C─C Bond Formation From Aldehydes via HFIP‐Assisted Hosomi‐Sakurai Methallylation
item.description:
A solvent-assisted, Lewis acid-free Hosomi–Sakurai reaction of aldehydes is reported. The method enables efficient C─C bond formation under mild conditions with broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and simple product isolation. Mechanistic and computational studies reveal that HFIP promotes the transformation through dual activation by enhancing aldehyde electrophilicity and stabilizing the post-addition intermediate.


ABSTRACT

The formation of carbon–carbon bonds is a cornerstone of organic synthesis, with the Hosomi-Sakurai reaction serving as a powerful tool for introducing allyl groups to carbonyl compounds. Traditionally, this transformation relies on Lewis acid catalysis to activate the carbonyl substrate. Here, we report a solvent-assisted, catalyst-free Hosomi-Sakurai reaction of aldehydes, providing a direct, atom-economical and operationally simple route to allylated products under mild conditions at room temperature. This method exhibits broad substrate scope, including aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, and proceeds with high chemoselectivity and functional group tolerance. Mechanistically, HFIP acts as a dual facilitator: it activates the aldehyde via hydrogen bonding, enhancing its electrophilicity, while simultaneously stabilizing the intermediate formed after allylsilane addition, thereby promoting the reaction and eliminating the need for external catalysts, additives, or Lewis acids.

item.title: Titanium‐Catalyzed 2‐Selective C─H Alkenylation of Pyridines With Alkynes
item.description:
2-Alkenylpyridines are formed regio- and stereoselectively from pyridines and internal alkynes by C─H bond activation reactions achieved in the presence of titanium catalyst IndTiBn3 (Ind = η 5-indenyl) and the Lewis acid [Ph3C][B(C6F5)4].


ABSTRACT

First examples of titanium-catalyzed C─H-addition reactions of pyridines to symmetrical and unsymmetrical internal alkynes, which lead to highly substituted alkenylpyridines, are described. The reactions take place exclusively at the 2-position of the pyridine, and both aryl- and alkyl-substituted alkynes are successfully converted. In most cases, the new reaction takes place with excellent stereoselectivity, leading to E-configurated 2-alkenylpyridines exclusively. Only in two exceptional cases, products with the opposite configuration of the double bond are formed selectively. When unsymmetrical alkynes are used, both possible regioisomers are formed in ratios of approximately 1:1. The active catalyst is prepared in situ from the heteroleptic titanium complex IndTiBn3 (Ti3) and the Lewis acid Ph3C[B(C6F5)4].

item.title: Crystallization‐Driven Self‐Assembly of Polymers and Emerging Technologies
item.description:
Crystallization-driven self-assembly provides a powerful tool for crystalline polymeric nanostructures with controlled dimensions, anisotropic morphologies, and well-defined internal order. By linking molecular packing and crystallization behavior with nucleation, growth, morphology regulation, characterization, and application, this review highlights how crystallization governs the formation, structure and function of polymeric assemblies.


ABSTRACT

Crystallization plays an important role in polymer self-assembly by directing molecular packing, internal ordering, and morphology regulation. The emergence of crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) has provided a powerful strategy for constructing polymer nanostructures with controlled dimensions, anisotropic morphologies, and desired functions. This review focuses on the CDSA of polymers and emerging technologies, with emphasis on the mechanistic roles of crystallization in nucleation and growth, as well as the regulation of their morphology and functions by molecular design and external parameters such as concentration, solvent, temperature, light, and pH. We also summarize representative characterization methods and simulations used to reveal the CDSA of polymers, and highlight potential applications in biomedicine, optoelectronics, anti-counterfeiting, information storage, and catalysis. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities in CDSA and emerging strategies are discussed.

item.title: Hydrophilicity and Electrostatic Complementarity Controlled Substrate Selectivity of Enzymes Inside Reverse Micelles
item.description:
Polymeric enzyme nanoreactor demonstrating photo-responsive crosslinking to tune reaction kinetics. Charged polymer backbone offers altered substrate selectivity through complementary electrostatic interactions.


ABSTRACT

Harnessing enzymes for synthetic processes in non-native environments while maintaining selectivity across different substrates is challenging. Here, we report amphiphilic random copolymers that self-assemble into reverse micelles, which can then sequester enzymes to form nanoreactors and maintain catalytic activity in organic solvents. Photo-responsive functional groups in scaffold design offer spatial and temporal control over crosslinking density and reaction kinetics. Variations in pK a and density of charged functional groups were explored to improve protein-polymer complexation as well as induce charge-based selectivity. A library of peptide substrates varying in partition coefficient, charge, and specificity constants has been synthesized to further delineate the driving force for selectivity. The findings here provide insights on structural factors for polymeric assemblies to enhance substrate selectivity without altering enzyme structure under non-native conditions.

item.title: Designed Construction of One‐Dimensional Positional‐Isomeric Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks for Asymmetric Aldol Catalysis
item.description:
Two one-dimensional positional-isomeric chiral 4-L-DTP-BFPPQ and 5-L-DTP-BFPPQ COFs were constructed via a positional-isomerism strategy. As asymmetric aldol catalysts, 4-L-DTP-BFPPQ exhibited superior enantioselectivity (87%–92%) over 5-L-DTP-BFPPQ (62%–78%), likely due to the positional effects on packing and chiral microenvironment.


ABSTRACT

Chiral covalent organic frameworks (COFs) represent a versatile platform for heterogeneous asymmetric catalysis. However, constructing positional-isomeric chiral COFs by regulating the position of chiral moieties to enhance their asymmetric catalytic performance remains a significant challenge. In this study, two V-shaped positional-isomeric chiral monomers, namely 4-L-DTP-Boc and 5-L-DTP-Boc, were designed and synthesized using naturally occurring L-proline as the chiral source. Subsequent condensation with 4,4′,4′′,4′′′-(pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetrayl)tetraaniline (BFPPQ) and Boc deprotection afforded two one-dimensional (1D) positional-isomeric chiral COFs (4-L-DTP-BFPPQ and 5-L-DTP-BFPPQ). The resulting chiral COFs were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts for asymmetric aldol reactions. Remarkably, 4-L-DTP-BFPPQ COF exhibited superior catalytic performance, particularly in terms of enantioselectivity (87%–92%), significantly outperforming 5-L-DTP-BFPPQ COF (62%–78%). The distinct catalytic behaviors of two chiral COFs could be attributed to the synergistic effects of chiral-unit positioning on packing behavior and local chiral microenvironment. These findings establish a correlation between regioisomerism in 1D chiral COFs and their asymmetric catalytic performance, providing a blueprint for the rational design of heterogeneous chiral COF catalysts.

item.title: Upcycling Post‐Harvest Soybean Straw Into FeCo Alloy‐Embedded N, S Co‐Doped Carbon as Electrocatalysts for Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
item.description:
Soybean straw-derived N/S co-doped carbon with FeCo alloy and Fe/Co-Nx sites enables efficient ORR/OER dual-catalysis for high-performance zinc-air batteries.


ABSTRACT

The sluggish kinetics of oxygen reduction and evolution reactions (ORR/OER) at air cathodes restrict the practical performance of rechargeable zinc–air batteries (ZABs), driving the urgent demand for low-cost, robust non-noble metal bifunctional electrocatalysts. Abundant agricultural soybean straw, featuring native porous frameworks and abundant oxygenated functional groups, represents a promising carbon substrate that facilitates electrolyte penetration and homogeneous immobilization of catalytic active sites. Herein, we report a facile ZnCl2-assisted pyrolysis strategy to fabricate FeCo alloy nanoparticles embedded within N, S co-doped biomass-derived carbon (denoted FeCo@NSC-900) via the high-value upcycling of waste soybean straw. Enabled by the multi-component synergistic effect between FeCo alloys, heteroatom coordination sites and porous carbon matrix, the as-synthesized FeCo@NSC-900 exhibited outstanding bifunctional electrocatalytic activity: it delivered an ORR half-wave potential of 0.880 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). When assembled as the air cathode of rechargeable ZABs, FeCo@NSC-900 afforded a peak power density of 211.26 mW cm−2 and a specific capacity of 798.60 mAh g−1 at 10 mA cm−2. More importantly, the assembled battery achieved remarkable cycling stability over 160 h. This study offers a sustainable design paradigm for converting waste agricultural biomass into bifunctional air electrodes.

item.title: Total Synthesis and Absolute Configuration of the Irregular Tetraterpene Viaticene A
item.description:
Viaticenes are tetraterpenes with a unique [6+2]-connectivity from the springtail Hypogastrura viatica. Here, we report a modular 13-step total synthesis of viaticene A, featuring stereoselective double-bond formation, a Cu-mediated allylic substitution, and Ni/Co-cocatalyzed vinyl-alkyl cross-electrophile coupling as key steps. NMR analysis of synthetic diastereomers enabled assignment of the natural viaticene A as all-R.


ABSTRACT

Viaticenes are tetraterpenes with a unique [6+2]-connectivity known from the epicuticular lipid layer of the springtail Hypogastrura viatica. Here, we report the total synthesis of viaticene A in thirteen steps from methyl 5-hexynoate, with an overall yield of 16%. Key steps in the construction of the core fragment include the stereoselective introduction of the E- and Z-double bonds via silyl- and carbocupration, respectively, and establishment of the central stereogenic center using pseudoephedrine as a chiral auxiliary. Subsequently, C9- and C11-alkyl building blocks are coupled to the core fragment via copper-mediated allylic substitution and nickel/cobalt-cocatalyzed vinyl–alkyl cross-electrophile coupling, preventing double-bond migration in the latter reaction with the novel additive combination styrene/water/molecular sieves. The modular synthesis route gives selective access to relevant diastereomers, allowing determination of the absolute configuration of viaticene A. Configurations at C-3, C-7, and C-19 are elucidated through careful analysis of the 13C-NMR spectra, assigning the all-R-configuration to the natural product.

item.title: Rational Ligand Design of Air‐Stable Ni–NHC Precatalysts for Challenging C─N Bond Formation: Balancing Steric Demand and Reactivity
item.description:
How bulky is too bulky for nickel? We explore how NHC steric modification controls the performance of Ni–NHC precatalysts for C─N bond formation. Increasing N-aryl bulk and NHC backbone chlorination enhance reactivity and selectivity, but excessive steric demand becomes detrimental. These results highlight the importance of a balanced steric environment that promotes productive reactivity while maintaining substrate accessibility.


ABSTRACT

A series of air-stable Ni(II)–NHC precatalysts (NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene) was developed for metal-catalyzed amination through systematic steric and electronic ligand evaluation. Chlorination of the NHC backbone, together with varying N-aryl bulk flanking the Ni center, enabled precise control over catalyst reactivity and selectivity, revealing the importance of a balanced steric approach in optimizing nickel catalysts for this purpose. Increased steric demand within this tailored ligand framework enhanced catalytic performance by facilitating reductive elimination and suppressing competing β-hydride elimination pathways, while maintaining sufficient accessibility for substrate coordination. This structure–reactivity relationship revealed a rational pairing of NHC sterics and substrate structure. This illustrates a divergence of reactivity patterns with Pd–NHC catalysts where increasing ligand bulk invariably yielded better cross-coupling outcomes, regardless of substrate size.

item.title: Enol/Enamine‐Mediated Asymmetric Synthesis Beyond Central Chirality
item.description:
Enols and enamines are versatile intermediates in asymmetric synthesis. This Review highlights the past decade's progress in utilizing them to build stereochemical frameworks beyond central chirality, including axial, inherent, helical, and mechanically planar chirality. Organized by catalytic activation modes—chiral amines, NHCs, CPAs, phase-transfer catalysts, and metal complexes—we provide a systematic, critical analysis of emerging strategies, current trends, and remaining challenges.


ABSTRACT

The catalytic asymmetric construction of complex, enantioenriched molecules remains a fundamental aspect of contemporary synthetic chemistry. Enols and enamines, by virtue of their ambident nucleophilicity and planar prochiral α-carbon, function as exceptionally versatile intermediates in asymmetric synthesis. In light of the growing interest in stereochemical frameworks beyond central chirality, enol and enamine chemistry has been expanded to facilitate the synthesis of molecules with axial, inherent, helical, and mechanically planar chirality. This review surveys the remarkable progress made over the past decade in this field. It encompasses a variety of activation modes—including chiral amines, N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs), chiral phosphoric acids (CPAs), phase-transfer catalysts, and metal complexes—that enable precise stereocontrol. Structured according to catalytic systems, this review provides a critical and systematic analysis of emerging strategies, highlights current trends, and addresses the ongoing challenges within this rapidly evolving field.

item.title: Chiral Amide‐Enabled Iridium‐Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Amidation for the Synthesis of P‐Chiral Phosphorus Oxides
item.description:
A new class of chiral carboxamide ligands, in combination with an achiral [Ind*IrI2]2 catalyst, was reported to promote enantioselective C–H activation of diarylphosphine oxides using p-toluenesulfonyl azide. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions to afford a range of P-stereogenic phosphine oxides containing sulfonamide motifs in up to 75% yield and 94% ee.


ABSTRACT

The development of chiral ligands that enable efficient asymmetric C–H functionalization remains a central challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report a new class of chiral carboxamide ligands, in combination with an achiral [Ind*IrI2]2 catalyst, that promotes the enantioselective C–H activation of diarylphosphine oxides with p-toluenesulfonyl azide. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions to afford a range of P-stereogenic phosphine oxides featuring sulfonamide motifs in up to 75% yield and 94% ee. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated by the reduction of pentavalent phosphorus products to the corresponding P(III) compounds with complete stereochemical retention.

item.title: Remarkable Isomeric Effects on Near‐Infrared Absorption and Aromaticity of Core‐Modified Phthalocyanines Incorporating Two Phenolic Groups
item.description:
The anti- and syn-isomers of near-infrared-absorbing dihydroxydicarbahemiporphyrazine that exhibit large absorption changes over 550 nm by redox reactions have been developed. After oxidation, the anti-isomers adopt an 18π-electron aromatic structure, whereas a nonaromatic structure contributes significantly to the equilibrium of the syn-isomers.


ABSTRACT

Two regioisomers of redox-switchable near-infrared (NIR) absorbing phthalocyanine analogues, dihydroxydicarbahemiporphyrazines, have been synthesized and their structure-property relationships have been investigated. Both isomers were readily oxidized by oxidants, and the resulting two-electron oxidized forms exhibited remarkable isomeric effects. The two-electron oxidized forms of the anti-isomers exhibited distinct NIR absorption over 900 nm in chloroform, and the maximum wavelength change in the absorption spectra upon redox process was over 550 nm. In contrast, weak and broad bands were observed in the 500–1000 nm region for the corresponding syn-isomers. The 1H NMR spectra indicated the presence of diatropic ring current effect in the two-electron oxidized form of the anti-isomer with arylthio substituents. No such ring current effect was observed for the syn-isomer. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggested that a nonaromatic asymmetric tautomer with a smaller static electric dipole moment plays a pivotal role in the optical properties and aromaticity in the syn-isomers.

item.title: Asymmetric Alternating‐Current Electrolysis for Deoxygenation of Benzylic Alcohols With Suppressed Anode Consumption
item.description:
In this article, an asymmetric AC-promoted direct deoxygenation of benzyl alcohol and related carbonyl compounds is reported, demonstrating how asymmetric waveform design expands the electrochemical window, enabling sustained high-potential operation while limiting anode weight loss to approximately stoichiometric requirements.


ABSTRACT

Sacrificial anodes in conventional direct current electrolysis suffer from rapid and irreversible consumption, limiting sustainability in reductive electrosynthesis. Herein, we report an asymmetric alternating current (AC) electrolysis protocol that enables direct deoxygenation of benzylic alcohols and related carbonyl compounds using water as the hydrogen source. By operating at 10 V, a potential that causes rapid anode failure under DC, the asymmetric waveform leverages periodic polarity reversal to partially recover anodically leached Zn2+ ions at the electrode surface and limit anode weight loss to approximately 5% per cycle. The method exhibits broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent chemoselectivity for benzylic C─O bonds. The protocol is also compatible with D2O, affording α-deuterated methylarenes with high isotope incorporation (typically over 90%). Mechanistic studies support a radical pathway in which Zn2+ facilitates the initial electron transfer.

item.title: Light‐Driven Photosensitive Materials Induce Lysosome Escape for Tumor Treatment
item.description:
This article summarizes the photosensitive materials alter lysosomal membrane permeability under light drive. These lysosome-targeted photosensitive materials could induce various death pathways of cell via photodynamic therapy or photothermal therapy. We hope that this review can provide guidance for optimizing delivery efficiency of tumor drug and promoting lysosomal-mediated tumor cell death precisely.


ABSTRACT

Lysosomes, as a key acidic organelle which was responsible for intracellular degradation and recycling, often intercept small-molecule drugs or nanoparticle drugs, limiting the therapeutic efficacy of cancer. To overcome this barrier, lysosomal rupture has emerged as a novel phototherapy strategy due to its noninvasive and spatiotemporally controllable nature. This review provides a comprehensive summary of photosensitive materials capable of modulating lysosomal membrane permeability upon light irradiation, focusing on two primary categories: nanomaterials and small molecules. These lysosome-targeting photosensitive materials can trigger multiple cell death pathways (apoptosis, necrosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis) by photodynamic or photothermal therapy, thereby enhancing drug escape and activating cell death cascades. The review aims to offer theoretical insights for optimizing tumor drug delivery efficiency and achieving precise lysosome-mediated tumor cell death.

item.title: Front Cover: Multi‐Scale Investigation of Supramolecular Organogels Assembled From Pt(II)‐Salphen Complexes
item.description: The Front Cover illustrates the formation of a supramolecular gel by the self-assembly of platinum complexes through Pt-Pt metallophilic interactions and p stacking to generate a fibrillar network that ultimately yields an emissive soft material. More details are provided in the Research Article by C. Guibert, G. Vives and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/chem.71506).

item.title: Self‐Immolative Poly(Benzyl Ether)s: Design Principles and Controlled Depolymerization
item.description:
Unzipping to Sustainability: This Concept article explores the thermodynamic design of quinone-methide (QM)-based poly(benzyl ether)s (PBEs). It explains how a low ceiling temperature (T c), QM stability, and an entropic gain drive rapid depolymerization (“unzipping”) of PBEs into monomers. Through modular end-cap design, these self-immolative polymers achieve precise, stimulus-responsive behavior, providing a robust platform for signal amplification and circular chemical recycling.


ABSTRACT

Self-immolative polymers (SIPs) constitute a sophisticated class of stimuli-responsive materials capable of undergoing complete end-to-end depolymerization upon a single triggering event. Among the various SIP architectures, quinone-methide (QM)-based poly(benzyl ether)s (PBEs) stand out owing to their high structural stability and well-defined disassembly kinetics. This article reviews the fundamental design principles of PBEs, emphasizing the thermodynamic role of their low ceiling temperature (T c) and their 1,6-elimination mechanism for depolymerization. It also demonstrates how the restoration of aromaticity and the entropic gain drive polymerization (“zipping”) of QM monomers and depolymerization (“unzipping”) of the polymer backbone into stable monomeric units, respectively. Furthermore, it discusses recent advances in modular end-cap engineering, which enable precise spatiotemporal control over depolymerization in response to chemical, photochemical, and biological stimuli. Overall, by highlighting the applications of PBEs in signal amplification, controlled cargo release, and the development of chemically recyclable materials, this article offers a comprehensive overview of their potential to redefine the boundaries of functional macromolecular design within a sustainable framework.

item.title: Recent Advances in Hierarchical Porous Organic Cages: From Discrete Structure to Integrated Assemblies
item.description:
This concept illustrates porous organic cages (POCs), with tunable cavities and modular design, act as intrinsic hosts and building blocks, hierarchically assembling from molecules to macroscopic structures.


ABSTRACT

In nature, functional complexity often arises from multiscale assembly across hierarchical levels. Inspired by this principle, porous organic cages (POCs), featuring well-defined intrinsic cavities, solution processability, and high chemical tunability, have emerged as versatile molecular platforms for multiscale materials engineering. This concept highlights representative examples in which POCs act as modular, shape-persistent building blocks within hierarchical assemblies, and elucidates how their confined cavities, solubility, and structural modularity enable the rational construction of sophisticated materials systems. At the molecular level, POCs function as enzyme-mimetic hosts that encapsulate and stabilize metal clusters (MCs) within discrete cavities. Benefiting from their structural tunability, POCs can also serve as bulky building blocks for integration into extended frameworks (e.g., COFs, MOFs, and supramolecular frameworks), as well as for the construction of nested host-in-host architectures and well-ordered multiscale crystalline materials. Such hierarchical assembly integrates structural advantages across length scales by preserving intrinsic porosity while introducing efficient mass and electron transport pathways, thereby enabling enhanced separation and catalytic performance. By translating bioinspired design principles into synthetic materials, these systems offer a programmable route towards multifunctional platforms.

item.title: Advances in Carbon‐Nitrogen Bond Formation From CO2 and Nitrogenous Small Molecules Through Tandem Electrocatalysis
item.description:
Utilizing greenhouse gas emissions and environmental contaminants as feedstocks offers a promising route for renewable energy storage and conversion, as well as the production of value-added chemicals. Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO2 with inorganic nitrogen species (e.g., N2, NO3 −, and NO2 −), enabled by efficient tandem catalysis, has emerged as an effective strategy to synthesize urea and other complex C─N bonded small molecules.


ABSTRACT

The electrocatalytic conversion of waste product molecules to valorized chemicals and fuels driven by clean energy is a promising approach to improving environmental health and alleviating the energy crisis. Historically, emphasis has been placed on CO2 sequestration and electroreduction, as it makes up most greenhouse gas emissions, however, products obtained from CO2 reduction are limited in variety. Coupling CO2 reduction with nitrogenous small molecules (N2, NO3 −, NO2 −, etc.) would expand the variety of valorized products while simultaneously increasing the removal of harmful environmental contaminants. In this review, the benefits of tandem catalysis promoting C─N bond coupling of CO2 and nitrogenous small molecules are compared to traditional single site catalysis. Various tandem catalytic systems have been reported toward the electrosynthesis of urea, exhibiting high yield rates and extended catalytic stability. Innovative approaches have also facilitated the electrosynthesis of other organonitrogen compounds, including acetamide, methylamine, and formamide. Overall, advancements in tandem electrocatalysis signify considerable progress toward sustainable chemical synthesis, energy conservation, and emission reduction.

item.title: Well‐Defined Nickel Precatalysts: Form, Function, and Application
item.description:
This review provides guidance on which nickel precatalysts to choose for a given application or which properties to prioritize in reaction development. A summary of the ease of synthesis, stability, diversity, accessibility, modularity, and general applicability is provided along with a related infographic.


ABSTRACT

Modern synthetic methods for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, fine chemicals, and agrochemicals have been revolutionized by the advent of cross-coupling chemistry. Well-defined palladium precatalysts have often been the mainstay for such reactions; however, more investigators are increasingly turning to Earth-abundant metals (EAMs), in particular nickel precatalysts. Nickel precatalysts have shown to allow for a broad substrate scope, they provide active species in variable oxidation states and demonstrate reactions that often proceed by unique mechanisms. This review will provide guidance on which nickel precatalysts to choose for a given application or which properties to prioritize in reaction development. Discussion points will cover the ease of synthesis, stability, diversity, accessibility, modularity, and general applicability.

item.title: Transition‐Metal‐Catalyzed Carbon‐Carbon Cross‐Coupling: Synthesis of α‐Chiral Allylic Amines
item.description:
α-Chiral allylic amines represent a privileged structure in organic synthesis, catalysis, and other areas. Thus, the development of catalytic methods for straightforward and efficient construction of chiral allylic amines has been a longstanding interest in synthetic chemistry. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in transition-metal-catalyzed carbon-carbon cross-coupling reaction for asymmetric chiral allylic amines synthesis, with an emphasis on catalytic strategy development and mechanistic insights.


ABSTRACT

α-Chiral allylic amines represent a privileged structure in organic synthesis, catalysis, and other areas. Thus, the development of catalytic methods for straightforward and efficient construction of chiral allylic amines has been a longstanding interest in synthetic chemistry. In this context, transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric carbon-carbon cross-coupling is evolving into an enabling and versatile platform for direct synthesis of α-chiral allylic amines. Thus, this review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in this dynamic area, highlighting key catalytic strategies and mechanistic insights for catalytic C─C bond-forming processes that underpin the streamlined synthesis of chiral allylic amine frameworks from easily available starting materials.

item.title: Well Dispersion of Nanoparticles by Surface Modification: Strategies and Biomedical Applications
item.description:
Nanoparticles tend to aggregate in physiological environments, severely limiting their biomedical applications. This review systematically summarizes the research progress and biomedical applications of three core strategies via surface modification (covalent modification, coordinating modification, and hydrophobic interaction-mediated modification) in enhancing the dispersion stability of nanoparticles. All three strategies inhibit aggregation by regulating nanoparticle surface properties, supporting applications in biomedical imaging, tumor therapy, and antibacterial/anti-infective treatments.


ABSTRACT

Nanoparticles tend to aggregate in physiological environments, severely limiting their biomedical applications. This review systematically summarizes the research progress and biomedical applications of three core strategies via surface modification (covalent modification, coordinating modification, and hydrophobic interaction-mediated modification) in enhancing the dispersion stability of nanoparticles. Covalent modification constructs stable interfaces via chemical bonds, coordinating modification optimizes dispersibility while endowing targeting/responsive functions, and hydrophobic interaction-mediated modification achieves efficient dispersion through noncovalent self-assembly. All three strategies inhibit aggregation by regulating nanoparticle surface properties, supporting applications in biomedical imaging, tumor therapy, and antibacterial/anti-infective treatments. Finally, future directions are prospected, focusing on multifunctional synergy, precision and intelligence, clinical translation, and interdisciplinary integration, providing references for the development of high-performance biomedical nanomaterials.

item.title: Rare‐Earth‐Based Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Electrochemical Energy Applications: Current Status and Emerging Opportunities
item.description:
RE-MOFs provide unique opportunities for electrochemical energy application owing to their tunable coordination environments and distinctive electronic structures. This review highlights recent advances in RE-MOF-based materials for batteries, Supercapacitors, and electrocatalysis, emphasizing structure-function relationships and emerging strategies for designing high-performance electrochemical energy systems.


ABSTRACT

Rare-earth-based metal-organic frameworks (RE-MOFs) have increasly emerged as a distinctive class of functional materials for electrochemical energy storage and conversion. The unique coordination chemistry of rare-earth ions, including high coordination numbers, shielded 4f electronic configurations, strong Lewis acidity, and accessible multivalent redox states in selected elements, endows RE-MOFs with exceptional framework stability, distinct redox functionality, and enhanced interfacial reactivity. This review comprehensively covers recent advances in RE-MOF-based materials for batteries, supercapacitors (SCs), and electrocatalysis. We first elucidate the fundamental coordination chemistry of rare-earth ions to establish the origins of their electrochemical functionality. We then focus on design strategies such as framework engineering, composite construction, and thermal transformation, emphasizing structure-property-performance correlations that link molecular-level features to macroscopic behavior. We critically assess key challenges, including mechanistic ambiguities, limited conductivity, scalability, and sustainability concerns. Finally, we propose future research directions, highlighting advanced characterization, artificial intelligence for accelerated discovery, systematic exploration of the lanthanide series, and sustainable preparation routes. This integrated perspective aims to guide the rational design and practical implementation of RE-MOFs for sustainable electrochemical energy technologies.

item.title: Cross‐Scale Coupling Perspective: A New Pathway to Break the Selectivity Dilemma of Electrocatalytic Energy Conversion Reactions
item.description:
This review establishes a full micro–meso–macro cross-scale coupling framework to resolve electrocatalytic selectivity dilemmas. It contrasts single-scale limits with multi-tier synergistic regulation, outlines adaptive, AI-driven design paths, and bridges lab catalytic performance to industrial high-current operation gaps.


ABSTRACT

Against the backdrop of global energy transition and carbon neutrality goals, electrocatalysis stands as a core technology for efficient conversion of renewable energy and green chemical synthesis, and its selectivity regulation has become a prominent research hotspot. Nevertheless, most existing studies focus merely on a single scale, such as atomic-level electronic structures or macroscopic mass transfer, while neglecting cross-scale synergistic regulation spanning from nanoactive sites to mesoscopic interfaces and further to macroscopic reactors. This renders the selectivity performance achieved under ideal laboratory conditions difficult to meet the complex dynamic requirements of industrial high-current-density and supported catalyst systems, giving rise to a distinct gap between fundamental research and industrial practical applications. This paper systematically reviews the regulation of electrocatalytic selectivity, aiming to construct a comprehensive theoretical framework for cross-scale selectivity regulation across macroscale, mesoscale, and nanoscale with full-scale coverage and in-depth elaboration. The research scope covers multiple levels, including active sites, interfacial environments, and external field responses. Future research should prioritize deepening the integration of artificial intelligence and electrocatalysis to enable intelligent catalyst design, develop self-adaptive catalyst systems to optimize dynamic reaction processes, and accelerate industrial applications in green hydrogen production, carbon dioxide conversion, and other related fields.

item.title: Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks (HOFs) for C2 Gas Separation and Purification
item.description:
Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) with customized pore size/shape and chemistry have overcome the conventional trade-off between adsorption capacity and separation selectivity, enabling highly efficient separation of C2 gases, including binary systems of C2H2/CO2, C2H2/C2H4, and C2H6/C2H4, as well as multicomponent systems of C2H2/CO2/C2H4, C2H2/C2H6/C2H4, and CH4/C2H4/C2H6/C3H6/C3H8/CO2/H2.


ABSTRACT

Industrial separation of C2 gas mixtures, particularly challenging C2H2/CO2, C2H2/C2H4, and C2H6/C2H4 separations, occupies a considerable portion of energy consumption in chemical production, highlighting the urgent need for low-carbon separation technologies. Adsorptive separation using functional porous materials provides a promising ambient-condition alternative to cut energy demand dramatically while maintaining high purification efficiency. Beyond the extensively studied metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) have emerged as a rising class of crystalline porous materials for hydrocarbon separation, thanks to their tunable framework chemistry, precisely engineered pore environments, facile solution processability, and excellent regeneration capability. These unique advantages have enabled HOFs to deliver competitive performance in demanding separation scenarios ranging from selective C2H2 capture to C2H6-selective olefin purification. Herein, we present a timely and comprehensive overview of recent advances in HOF-based sorbents for C2 gas separation and purification, covering conventional binary systems (C2H2/CO2, C2H2/C2H4, and C2H6/C2H4) as well as more complex multicomponent systems (three-component C2H2/CO2/C2H4, C2H2/ C2H6/C2H4, and seven-component CH4/C2H4/C2H6/C3H6/C3H8/CO2/H2). We further elucidate the critical structure–performance relationships governing different separation mechanisms and highlight key bottlenecks and future research directions to guide the development of HOFs for industrial gas separation.

item.title: Fibrilpaint: A Class of Amyloid‐Targeting Peptides
item.description:
FibrilPaints are modular peptides engineered to recognize amyloid fibrils. By systematically varying charge, sequence, and termini, their binding behavior can be tuned while retaining recognition. Successful binding ″paints″ fibrils for visualization and opens routes toward targeted degradation and diagnostic applications.


ABSTRACT

Amyloid fibrils are a common pathological hallmark in multiple neurodegenerative diseases, yet molecular tools to recognize and manipulate them remain scarce. We report FibrilPaints, a family of modular peptides designed for amyloid binding and adaptable chemical functionality. The degenerative amyloid-targeting unit of FibrilPaints, W5P4H3R2, has a high content of π-stacking and aromatic side chains. Systematic sequence variation, altering charge, termini, and residue order, revealed the importance of the composition of the amyloid-targeting unit for high-affinity binding across Tau and Huntingtin fibrils. Importantly, sequence changes outside this unit do not preclude fibril binding, which permits attachment of fluorophores or E3-recruiting motifs for targeted protein degradation. This work establishes FibrilPaint as a modular peptide system for binding Tau and Huntingtin amyloid fibrils, with potential for broader detection and modulation applications.

item.title: Thiosemicarbazone‐Based Responsive MRI Contrast Agents Activated Through a Change in CuII Binding Site on Albumin
item.description:
A τR -based CuII-responsive MRI contrast agent containing a thiosemicarbazone unit as a CuII-selective chelator has been designed, synthesized and evaluated. This work demonstrates that the agent can efficiently withdraw CuII from its native binding site in HSA and form CuII-bridged ternary complexes. This strategy allows a marked increase in relaxivity and provides a new strategy for CuII-responsive agents based on metal redistribution within biological macromolecules.


ABSTRACT

The development of copper-responsive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) probes remains limited by the scarcity of robust strategies capable of operating under physiological conditions and within complex biological environments. Here we report CuII-responsive MRI contrast agents (CAs) which are able to extract CuII from human serum albumin (HSA) and subsequently form ternary adducts. The CAs combine a GdIII-DO3A-monoamide complex linked to α-pyridyl thiosemicarbazone (pyrTSC) ligands, introduced here as innovative CuII binding units. The TSC units display strong CuII affinity and form ternary TSC–CuII–HSA adducts at a site distinct from the canonical ATCUN motif. Using UV-visible and EPR spectroscopies, we show that the CuII extraction and ternary adduct formation remain possible even in the presence of the Gd-binding moiety. The formation of ternary complexes enhances the rotational correlation time (τ R), leading to measurable increases in relaxivity for the various complexes. This work introduces a new strategy in which CuII-triggered protein binding is exploited to activate responsive MRI CAs, thereby broadening their chemical space.

item.title: In Situ Construction of Co‐Modified Ni/Ni3P@C Heterostructures via MOF‐Derived Internal Phosphorus Source Engineering for Efficient and Stable Overall Water Splitting
item.description:
